## What the function does

`composeTwoSpendingInstances` takes the caller's `Graph` plus two independently prepared `SpendingCreationInputs` values and two render callbacks. It binds one shared immutable defaults object (`{ name: "alerts-a", diagnostics: "off" }`) through `spendingAlertsFor(graph, defaults)` (examples/spending-alerts/causal-entry.ts:49-51), then calls `preset.compose(...)` twice. The first compose inherits the defaults; the second passes per-compose overrides `{ name: "alerts-b", diagnostics: "summary" }` (causal-entry.ts:52-53, 36-45). Each returned `app.view` is the original five-port view object (causal-preset.ts:171-178) and is passed to `mountSpendingView(view, render)` (causal-view-binding.ts:17-20), which returns a stop function that ends observation only (causal-view-binding.ts:16, 32-36). The function returns both instances and both cleanup functions. It does not open resources, invent input facts, or invoke a transport; it only composes and observes.

## What the application must retain after either display is unmounted

Detaching a panel stops observation only: `stop()` unsubscribes the five port subscriptions and nothing else (causal-view-binding.ts:32-36). The README states plainly that panel detach stops observation while the running instance retains outstanding obligations (README.md:143), and that the application must preserve retained request records instead of treating panel cleanup as recovery (README.md:150-151). So after unmount the application must keep:

- The owning `Graph` and each original composed instance (`app.owner`, `app.inspect`, `app.runEndReady`, `app.built`) — the demo keeps `app.owner` and `app.inspect` (causal-graded-demo.ts:65, 140-143, 185-188).
- The original `.view` and the original issued capabilities (`app.capabilities`, including `retained.execution`), because frameworks pass the original identity/execution/retained handles and the retained lineage must stay the same object (causal-graded-demo.ts:85-87, 121-124, 283-287; README.md:91-96).
- The host's retained request/admission/outcome records: the host keeps a bounded `records` map (causal-focused-host.ts:140, 47-51) and the README says the application must preserve those records (README.md:125-132, 146-151). A pending or unknown outcome is not success and is not proof of no submission (README.md:149-150).
- The two prepared `SpendingResource` objects and their bindings: each resource is claimed once per host epoch (`resource.claim()`, causal-focused-host.ts:96; causal-resource.ts:69-72) and the lease is transferred to the graph (causal-focused-host.ts:110). The resource binding must match the instance binding (causal-focused-host.ts:76-77).
- The two sets of input Nodes: `spendingInputNodes` requires six distinct input nodes per instance (causal-preset.ts:73-93), and the host wires them as declared edges (causal-focused-host.ts:88-94).
- The publication/evidence references used for correlation: `app.view.publication.cache` and the exact `authorityId` from that instance's publication (README.md:106-123), plus the request references (README.md:128).

## What the distinct names, independently prepared input Nodes, and resource bindings contribute

- **Distinct names** are identity/labelling only. `name` is validated as a bounded string (causal-entry.ts:41-42) and is used to prefix every node name (`${name}/startup`, `${name}/causal/...`, `${name}/publication`, and `${name}/diagnosticSummary` only when diagnostics is `summary`) (causal-preset.ts:60-72; causal-focused-host.ts:81-87). The README is explicit: a name is not an authorization token, and changing `name` does not clone input Nodes, create an independent resource or rewrite its binding (README.md:85-89). Distinct names keep the two instances' node namespaces and authority IDs separate in the shared Graph (causal-focused-host.ts:310; causal-publication.ts:411).
- **Independently prepared input Nodes** are the actual per-instance facts. Each instance must receive its own six distinct input nodes (causal-preset.ts:73-93); the host declares them as its input edges (causal-focused-host.ts:88-94) and each node's `checkInput` validates the frame against that instance's binding (causal-inputs.ts:352-377, 377). Sharing a node between instances would make the two instances read the same facts and would fail the distinct-node check (causal-preset.ts:91-92).
- **Resource bindings** are the per-instance destination/epoch identity. `composeSpendingHost` validates the raw binding and requires `same(resource.binding, binding)` (causal-focused-host.ts:74-77); the binding carries `packRef`, `sourceDigest`, `runtimeDigest`, `destinationRef`, `compositionEpoch`, `hostEpoch` (causal-inputs.ts:14-17, 212-225). Admission matches grants to `binding.destinationRef`, `binding.hostEpoch` and `binding.compositionEpoch` (causal-admission.ts:253-261), and the publication join checks the authority ID and binding epoch (causal-publication.ts:454-462). So the binding is what makes each instance's writes and evidence belong to that instance's resource; the second instance in the demo uses a distinct binding with `compositionEpoch: 2`, `hostEpoch: 2` and its own resource (causal-graded-demo.ts:89-114).

## Notes on scope

This snippet is not executed. It does not open resources, invent input facts, or call a transport; the caller supplies the Graph, both prepared inputs and both resources. Normal host behavior (including its simulated writer) is left intact. The two instances share the Graph and the immutable defaults, but not their input Nodes, resources or running state (README.md:88-89).
